thread.title: Trump Tax Cuts Boost Dividend Payouts Most Since 2012; Record Buybacks?

author: BILL PETERS
title: Trump Tax Cuts Boost Dividend Payouts Most Since 2012; Record Buybacks?
text:
Dividend payouts announced by S&P 500 companies have increased by a net $14.7 billion so far this year, setting up the biggest first-quarter bump since 2012, as the strong economy and President Trump's tax cuts swell corporate coffers.
X Meanwhile, share buybacks could see a record year in 2018, with potential to top the 2007 high of $589.1 billion and surge from 2017's total of $518.7 billion. In addition to lowering the corporate tax rate to 21% from 35%, the tax overhaul also made it cheaper to bring profits made overseas back to the U.S.
Apple ( AAPL ) alone is expected to repatriate $245 billion in foreign profits over the coming years , raising hopes that the iPhone maker could use some of the cash to bump up shareholder returns. Morgan Stanley said in November that Apple, Microsoft ( MSFT ), General Electric ( GE ), Pfizer ( PFE ) and IBM ( IBM ) have the most "accumulated foreign earnings."
The $14.7 billion dividend increase in Q1 is up sharply from the $9.7 billion in gains seen a year ago but still well short of 2012's increase of $22.4 billion, when the economy was still rebounding.
"The bull market was started in March 2009," said Howard Silverblatt, senior index analyst at S&P Dow Jones Indices, in an interview. "Companies waited a little while to make sure it was real before they started increasing."
And with only a few days left in Q1, 130 S&P 500 companies increased their dividends over that time, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices. No company has cut its dividend, potentially marking the first Q1 with no decreases since at least 2003.
"Dividends are typically event driven," Silverblatt said. "... And we don't have that many negative events here."
Apple fell 2.6% in the stock market today , while Microsoft tumbled 4.6%, both falling back below their 50-day moving averages. GE jumped 4.3% from a long-time low on rumors that Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKB ) was buying a stake. Pfizer slipped 0.1%. IBM dipped 0.9%.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Dividend Leaders: Energy, Consumer Sectors So far in Q1, some of the biggest dividend hikes have come from the energy sector. Many energy companies pulled back on payouts due to the oil-price crash that began in 2014. But companies that fall into the health care, consumer-discretionary and tech sectors also hiked their payouts.
Home Depot ( HD ) in February announced a 15.7% quarterly dividend increase. Best Buy ( BBY ) hiked its own by 32%. Yum Brands ( YUM ) in January OK'd a 20% dividend increase.
In health care, AbbVie ( ABBV ) announced a 35% jump in its dividend payout. Chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) announced a 10% increase to its quarterly dividend in January.
Dividend payouts from S&P 500 companies already reached a record $109.5 billion in Q4, S&P Dow Jones Indices said in a release last week. In December, aerospace giant Boeing ( BA ) announced a 20% boost in its dividend, but GE halved its dividend in November.
Even as the economy improves, Trump's plans to hit some imports with tariffs continue to agitate investors.
"If costs go up, you've got to either raise prices or eat some of the profit, or a combination of the two," Silverblatt said.
